brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.

requirements.evidence: Centre hex base piece:0,0,0 plus six surrounding full hex bases at (1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1),(1,-1),(-1,1), all at level 0 (7 piece parts).

requirements.requirement: Stands on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet
requirements.evidence: Three addSpike ops with variant stud and facing down at level-0 junctions: (-1,0)/(-1,1)/(0,0), (0,-1)/(0,0)/(1,-1), and (0,0)/(0,1)/(1,0). They form a spread triangle under the honeycomb. Caps closed the open faces and lockJoints was applied; check_build is ok with meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell hex honeycomb (centre cell plus six ring cells, one level) standing on three downward-facing stud spikes at spread-out junctions. Open faces are capped and joints locked. check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear. I did not add props or soil since the brief is about structure only. Note: the spikes are three; the configurator would accept more, but three meets the 'at least three' requirement.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
